We show that this new loss function boosts performance, with the most prominent improvement occurring when p ≈ 3 p\approx 3 . Each modification was tested individually against a “default” version of the algorithm in which each entry in 𝑿 \boldsymbol{X} was drawn independently from the Standard Normal distribution and the loss function was the default loss function described in the introduction. See Appendix B for more details on the default algorithm. For all GNN-based algorithms in this paper, we used 200 200 features for the initial embedding and for the output of all but the final layer, and we used the AdamW optimizer with default learning rate 0.001 0.001 . In our initial experiments, we found that increasing the number of features per layer only ever improved performance, that changing the learning rate did not substantially change performance as long as the algorithm converged, and that using vanilla gradient descent rather than Adam or AdamW was detrimental due to the former not scaling gradients. Since we are interested in methods that perform well in the general purpose, the performance of each modification was tested on Erdős-Rényi graphs.
